title: About Us for Republican Voters
one_liner: Who this door is for: voters who vote Republican and the broader political right, building their own package in their own language.
scope_in: Who the audience is; that this is not a general-audience site; the promise that your side builds its own package here; why a neutral visitor goes to the .io instead.
scope_out: The mechanics of any plank below; anything addressed to the D, L or S audiences.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Is this site for me?

title: A Replacement for TPUSA
one_liner: We say plainly that we are working to be a replacement for TPUSA — a claim that exists only on this door.
scope_in: The slot we fill; same organizing job, different method (meritocracy and community voting rather than a small group announcing downward); who does not fund us and who does not control us.
scope_out: The same claim on any other door or on the .io — it appears nowhere else, by rule.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What are you a replacement for?

title: Replacing Incumbents Controlled by Global Elites
one_liner: The core action: get political challengers elected to replace incumbents controlled by global elites and the Deep State.
scope_in: Elections as the mechanism; challengers first and incumbent protection never; the non-citizen powerful forces we name as the threat, domestic and foreign.
scope_out: Naming individual people we cannot substantiate — we name the category, not the person.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who exactly are you trying to replace, and how?

title: Meritocracy: Finding the Best Candidates
one_liner: The engine underneath everything: surface the candidates most dedicated to citizens and strongest at refusing to be co-opted.
scope_in: Dedication measured after election rather than promised before it; the strength to refuse capture once in office; matching candidates to where a voter sits on the political spectrum.
scope_out: The trust-score arithmetic itself, which is its own area.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How do you decide who is 'best' without just picking favorites?

title: Great Ethics, Like Christian Ethics
one_liner: This door talks about great ethics and names Christian ethics — deliberately, and exclusively here.
scope_in: Why the language belongs on this door; why the .io and the D, L and S doors carry no religion at all; the rule that two audiences never share a page.
scope_out: Any religion on any other door or on the non-partisan site.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Where do your ethics come from?

title: Removing the Rigged Economy
one_liner: The Republican voter's own package for removing the rigged layer and getting back to an ethical, clean economy.
scope_in: A goal shared by all four doors but written here by Republican voters in their own language; the package built by community voting; the destination — an economy that is ethical, clean and ideal for workers.
scope_out: The other three doors' versions of the same package.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What is your economic plan?

title: Community-Based Voting and Collaboration
one_liner: The mechanism the whole platform runs on: positions, plans and candidate judgments come from citizens voting and working together.
scope_in: The community builds the package rather than receiving it; voting on where you sit on the political spectrum; how that keeps a loud minority from being mistaken for the whole.
scope_out: The platform-wide reasoning engine, which lives in the main app.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who decides what this community stands for?

title: Fix Bills and Laws
one_liner: Partisan law work happens on the .com doors, and this is where Republican voters add and prioritize the laws they care about.
scope_in: Adding the laws this community cares about; the specific standing bills it cares about most; measuring a candidate against a concrete bill rather than a general statement.
scope_out: Law work on the .io — the non-partisan site does not host it.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Do you have actual legislation?

title: Fully Exposing the Deep State, Global Elites and the Epstein Class
one_liner: Citizens cannot fix what they are not allowed to see, so exposure comes before reform.
scope_in: The unelected layer as a first-class target; a sourced, citizen-readable record; gaps marked as gaps rather than filled in with a guess.
scope_out: Accusations we cannot substantiate, and naming a person where we can only prove a category.
newcomer_question_it_answers: What is actually being hidden from me?

title: US Intelligence Answers to US Citizens
one_liner: US intelligence services answer to US citizens, or they are not ours.
scope_in: Preventing an agency from deciding an election outcome; ending leverage over officeholders as a mechanism of capture; oversight a citizen can verify.
scope_out: Foreign services, which are the next area.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Can an agency decide my election?

title: Foreign Intelligence: No Puppet Master Over US Citizens
one_liner: A foreign service steering US politics is the purest form of the thing this door exists to stop.
scope_in: Narrative control over who gets elected; documenting the mechanism — funding, placed media, coordinated accounts, captured staff; foreign leverage on an officeholder as disqualifying.
scope_out: Domestic services, which are the previous area.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Is somebody outside the country picking my representatives?

title: Removing Voter Fraud for Good
one_liner: A citizen has to be able to believe the count, and the goal is structurally impossible fraud rather than fraud merely investigated.
scope_in: Every step from registration to certification checkable by an ordinary citizen; open, auditable technology so nobody has to trust a vendor; measuring candidates on whether they will vote for it.
scope_out: Any claim of a specific fraud we cannot source.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Can I trust the count?

title: No Needless or Forever Wars, and No Draft
one_liner: Wars that serve global elites rather than citizens are exactly what this door opposes, and citizens are not raw material for someone else's foreign policy.
scope_in: Forever wars as a symptom of captured incumbents; no draft; measuring candidates on their actual war votes rather than their speeches.
scope_out: A full foreign-policy doctrine — this is the plank, not the doctrine.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Where do you stand on war?

title: No China-Style Social Credit in America
one_liner: A score that decides what a citizen is allowed to do never gets built here — including the private-sector versions of it.
scope_in: Debanking, de-platforming as punishment, and scoring citizens by political behavior; measuring candidates on whether they will outlaw it before it arrives.
scope_out: The movement's own trust scores, which are about candidates, never about citizens.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Could a social credit system happen here?

title: Trust Scores
one_liner: Trust scores are how a citizen judges whether a candidate really works for citizens — built and voted here, at the party level.
scope_in: Republicans building and voting the scores for their own candidates; what the scoring reflects; the read-only roll-up that appears on the non-partisan site.
scope_out: Voting on the .io — the roll-up there is read-only and nobody votes on it.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Where do I cast a vote that counts on a candidate?

title: Our Board of Directors
one_liner: A real governance body that sits at the .com level, described accurately and never overstated.
scope_in: Why partisan governance belongs with the partisan community; the split between the .io's single high-level plan and the many partisan plans under this board.
scope_out: A board on the non-partisan side — there is none.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Who governs this?

title: Yearly Conference on Political Right Strategy
one_liner: The right's yearly strategy conference, standing in the slot AmFest holds today, where this community sets its direction together.
scope_in: A .com-level event that each party door runs its own version of; the speaker list as the test — people who represent citizens, never people placed there by global elites or the donor class.
scope_out: Describing it as a movement-wide non-partisan event.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Do you hold events?

title: Open Source, Open Data, Open AI
one_liner: Nobody has to trust us, because nobody can check a black box — every layer that decides something about a candidate or a vote is open to inspection.
scope_in: Open source code for the voting, matching and scoring; open data so a citizen can re-run the numbers; open AI method so a citizen can see why it concluded what it concluded and disagree.
scope_out: A citizen's own local files, which are private by design and said so plainly.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Why should I believe your numbers?

title: How This Door Relates to the Other Three
one_liner: Four party doors, one app: R Republicans, D Democrats, L Libertarians, S Democratic Socialists.
scope_in: WeCitizensR.com as edition R recognized by hostname; R and D mirroring on the partisan axis and L and S on the economic axis; the .io sending a visitor to the door they care about.
scope_out: Any attack on the voters behind another door — their captured incumbents are fair game, they are not.
newcomer_question_it_answers: Is this a Republican-only movement?

title: Words We Use and Words We Avoid
one_liner: Language is the whole job of this door: two audiences never share a page, and we never claim a status we do not hold.
scope_in: The phrases that belong here — replacement for TPUSA, political challengers, meritocracy, the rigged economy, Christian values; the phrases that never appear — the non-partisan voice, attacks on other doors' voters, any promised outcome or claimed endorsement.
scope_out: Copy written for the .io or for the D, L or S audiences.
newcomer_question_it_answers: How should I talk about this?
